messages.author: c475b088b76c0d36
messages.subject: groupComparisonTMT warnings in MSstatsTMT
parts:
Hi MSstatsTMT team,

I'm using MSstatsTMT package to analyze our dataset, which contained 18 samples in 5 conditions (biological replicates included). They belonged to 1 mixture and there were no technical replicates. I ran groupComparisonTMT to compare groups of interest, and there were 5 warnings showed up:

Warning messages:
1: In anova.lm(fitted_model) : ANOVA F-tests on an essentially perfect fit are unreliable
2: In anova.lm(fitted_model) : ANOVA F-tests on an essentially perfect fit are unreliable
3: In anova.lm(fitted_model) : ANOVA F-tests on an essentially perfect fit are unreliable
4: In anova.lm(fitted_model) : ANOVA F-tests on an essentially perfect fit are unreliable
5: In anova.lm(fitted_model) : ANOVA F-tests on an essentially perfect fit are unreliable

I thought this meant that there were no replicates in the comparison. When I looked at the result file, there were 3 rows that showed 'SingleMeasurePerCondition' in the issue column. There were also a few rows with 'completeMissing' and 'oneConditionMissing'. The rest has no value in the issue column.

I wonder if I should be concerned about the 5 warnings that showed up. The 5 warnings did not seem connected to the 3 rows with 'SingleMeasurePerCondition'. I'm not sure what that really meant.

I would really appreciate your help. Thank you so much for your time!

Best,
Hongya

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: groupComparisonTMT warnings in MSstatsTMT
parts:
Hi Hongya,

I believe these warnings were caused by the `SingleMeasurePerCondition` rows. When there is only one measurement the statistical model cannot estimate a standard error and thus the F-tests are unreliable. The rest of the models without a value in the `issue` column should be fine.

Best,
Devon
